Rolling training load

Source: R/descriptors.R
rolling_load.Rd

Computes, for every day, the sum and the mean of the daily loads over a window of window days, within each athlete (MODELS.md, M-11).

Usage

rolling_load(x, window = 7, same_day_load = c("include", "exclude"))

Arguments

x

A daily_load object, from as_daily_load(). It is checked first; an object changed after it was built (for example by subsetting) must be rebuilt with as_daily_load().

window

Length of the window in days, a single whole number >= 1.

same_day_load

Whether the window ends on the current day ("include", the default) or on the previous day ("exclude").

Value

A data frame with one row per row of x, in the same order, and the columns athlete, date, load, rolling_sum and rolling_mean. The attributes window and same_day_load record the arguments used.

Formula

For the daily loads \(w(1), \dots, w(T)\) of one athlete and a window of \(k\) days:

  • same_day_load = "include" (the default): the window ends on the current day, $$S(t) = \sum_{j = t-k+1}^{t} w(j),$$ defined for \(t \ge k\);

  • same_day_load = "exclude": the window ends on the previous day, $$S(t) = \sum_{j = t-k}^{t-1} w(j),$$ defined for \(t \ge k + 1\). This is the form of Carey et al. (2017, Eq. 1).

The rolling mean is \(S(t) / k\). The two options are related by "exclude" on day \(t\) = "include" on day \(t - 1\).

Timing option and default

The default is same_day_load = "include" (DECISIONS.md, D-021). This differs from the impulse-response models, whose default is "exclude" (D-012).

Missing and rest days

A day with a missing load makes every window that contains it NA (D-016); missing loads are never filled. Windows that do not fit in the series (the first \(k - 1\) days with "include", the first \(k\) with "exclude") are NA: there are no partial windows. Rest days count as load 0. Days added by as_daily_load() count as rest or as missing according to its gaps argument.

Acute

chronic workload ratio: Ratios of rolling loads and EWMA-based loads are not provided here: see the ACWR package (DECISIONS.md, D-019).

References

Carey DL, Blanch P, Ong K-L, et al. (2017). Training loads and injury risk in Australian football—differing acute:chronic workload ratios influence match injury risk. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 51, 1215-1220.

See also

monotony_strain(), srpe_load(), as_daily_load().

Examples

x <- as_daily_load(
  data.frame(date = as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:9,
             load = c(300, 0, 450, 500, 0, 0, 620, 410, 380, 0)),
  date = "date", load = "load"
)
rolling_load(x, window = 3)
#>    athlete       date load rolling_sum rolling_mean
#> 1        1 2026-01-01  300          NA           NA
#> 2        1 2026-01-02    0          NA           NA
#> 3        1 2026-01-03  450         750     250.0000
#> 4        1 2026-01-04  500         950     316.6667
#> 5        1 2026-01-05    0         950     316.6667
#> 6        1 2026-01-06    0         500     166.6667
#> 7        1 2026-01-07  620         620     206.6667
#> 8        1 2026-01-08  410        1030     343.3333
#> 9        1 2026-01-09  380        1410     470.0000
#> 10       1 2026-01-10    0         790     263.3333
rolling_load(x, window = 3, same_day_load = "exclude")
#>    athlete       date load rolling_sum rolling_mean
#> 1        1 2026-01-01  300          NA           NA
#> 2        1 2026-01-02    0          NA           NA
#> 3        1 2026-01-03  450          NA           NA
#> 4        1 2026-01-04  500         750     250.0000
#> 5        1 2026-01-05    0         950     316.6667
#> 6        1 2026-01-06    0         950     316.6667
#> 7        1 2026-01-07  620         500     166.6667
#> 8        1 2026-01-08  410         620     206.6667
#> 9        1 2026-01-09  380        1030     343.3333
#> 10       1 2026-01-10    0        1410     470.0000
